passages.text: Jesus said to His disciples, “It is inevitable that stumbling blocks will come, but woe to the one through whom they come!
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said that stumbling blocks will certainly come.
No one can prevent stumbling blocks from coming.
But great sorrow will come to the person who causes them.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν πλὴν οὐαὶ δι’ οὗ ἔρχεται

passages.text: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about causing others to stumble.
He said, “It is better for a person to have a large millstone tied around his neck.
It is better for that person to be thrown into the sea.
This is better than causing one of these little ones to stumble.”
passages.original: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα

passages.text: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them to be careful.
He said, “Watch yourselves.”
If your brother sins, rebuke him.
If your brother repents, forgive him.
passages.original: Προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ

passages.text: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He taught them about forgiveness.
If your brother sins against you, you must pay attention.
If he sins against you seven times in one day, you must notice it.
If he comes back to you seven times in that same day, you must listen to him.
If he says to you each time, “I repent,” you must forgive him each time.
You must forgive him every time he repents.
passages.original: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων Μετανοῶ ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ

passages.text: The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith!”
passages.sermon:
The apostles followed Jesus.
The apostles spoke to Jesus.
The apostles said, “Increase our faith!”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ Κυρίῳ Πρόσθες ἡμῖν πίστιν

passages.text: And the Lord answered, “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to his apostles.
He answered their request for more faith.
He said, "If you have faith."
Your faith can be very small.
It can be as small as a mustard seed.
You can speak to this mulberry tree.
You can say, 'Be uprooted.'
You can say, 'Be planted in the sea.'
The tree will obey you.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος Εἰ ἔχετε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως ἐλέγετε ἂν τῇ συκαμίνῳ ταύτῃ Ἐκριζώθητι καὶ φυτεύθητι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ καὶ ὑπήκουσεν ἂν ὑμῖν

passages.text: Which of you whose servant comes in from plowing or shepherding in the field will say to him, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He gave them an example.
He spoke about a servant and his master.
Suppose one of you has a servant.
The servant works in the field.
He plows or he shepherds.
The servant comes in from the field.
Will the master say to the servant, “Come at once and sit down to eat”?
passages.original: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε

passages.text: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?
passages.sermon:
A master has a servant.
The servant comes in from working in the field.
The master does not tell the servant to sit down and eat immediately.
Instead, the master gives the servant instructions.
The master says, "Prepare my meal."
The master says, "Dress yourself to serve me."
The master says, "Serve me while I eat and drink."
After the master finishes eating and drinking, the master allows the servant to eat and drink.
The servant eats and drinks only after serving the master.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ

passages.text: Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?
passages.sermon:
A master gives orders to his servant.
The servant obeys and does what the master commands.
The master does not thank the servant just because the servant obeyed.
The master expects the servant to do what he was told.
passages.original: μὴ ἔχει χάριν τῷ δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ διαταχθέντα

passages.text: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “You must obey everything God commands you.
After you obey, you must remember something important.
You should say, ‘We are unworthy servants.’
We only did what we had to do.
We only did our duty.”
passages.original: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν

passages.text: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.
passages.sermon: Jesus was traveling to Jerusalem.\r\nHe passed between Samaria and Galilee.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας

passages.text: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance and raised their voices, shouting, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered a village.
Ten men met Him.
These men had leprosy.
They stood far away from Jesus.
They called out loudly.
They said, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
passages.original: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν αὐτῷ δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες Ἰησοῦ Ἐπιστάτα ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς

passages.text: When Jesus saw them, He said, “Go, show yourselves to the priests.” And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the ten men who had leprosy.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Go. Show yourselves to the priests.”
The ten men began to go to the priests.
As they went, they became clean from leprosy.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν

passages.text: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back, praising God in a loud voice.
passages.sermon:
One of the ten lepers saw that he was healed.
He turned back.
He praised God.
He spoke with a loud voice.
passages.original: Εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.
passages.sermon: One man was a Samaritan.\r\nHe fell facedown at Jesus’ feet.\r\nHe thanked Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης

passages.text: “Were not all ten cleansed?” Jesus asked. “Where then are the other nine?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke.
He answered a question.
He said, “Were not all ten cleansed?”
He asked, “Where are the other nine?”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ

passages.text: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He asked a question.
He said, “Did no one return to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
Only this man, who was not a Jew, came back to thank God.
No others returned to praise God.
passages.original: οὐχ εὑρέθησαν ὑποστρέψαντες δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀλλογενὴς οὗτος

passages.text: Then Jesus said to him, “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man who returned.
Jesus said, "Stand up."
Jesus said, "Go on your way."
Jesus said, "Your faith has saved you."
passages.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀναστὰς πορεύου ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε

passages.text: When asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God would come, Jesus replied, “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees asked Jesus a question.
They wanted to know when the kingdom of God would come.
Jesus answered them.
He said the kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.
passages.original: Ἐπερωτηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν Φαρισαίων πότε ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν Οὐκ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ παρατηρήσεως

passages.text: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’ For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees.
The Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come.
Jesus answered them.
People will not say, “Look, here it is.”
People will not say, “Look, there it is.”
The kingdom of God is in your midst.
The kingdom of God is among you.
passages.original: οὐδὲ ἐροῦσιν Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ἤ Ἐκεῖ ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν

passages.text: Then He said to the disciples, “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Days will come.
You will desire to see one of the days of the Son of Man.
You will not see it.”
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε

passages.text: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about false reports.
People will say, “Look, there He is!”
People will also say, “Look, here He is!”
Do not go out to follow them.
Do not chase after these claims.
passages.original: καὶ ἐροῦσιν ὑμῖν Ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ ἤ Ἰδοὺ ὧδε μὴ ἀπέλθητε μηδὲ διώξητε

passages.text: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He called Himself the Son of Man.
The Son of Man will return one day.
On that day, everyone will see Him.
His coming will be clear to all people.
It will be like lightning.
Lightning flashes under the sky.
Lightning lights up the sky from one end to the other.
In the same way, the Son of Man will appear in His day.
No one will miss His coming.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἀστράπτουσα ἐκ τῆς ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰς τὴν ὑπ’ οὐρανὸν λάμπει οὕτως ἔσται ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of Man.\r\nHe must suffer many things first.\r\nThis generation will reject Him.
passages.original: πρῶτον δὲ δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης

passages.text: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.
passages.sermon:
In the days of Noah, people lived their normal lives.
They ate food.
They drank.
They married.
They gave others in marriage.
They did these things until the day Noah entered the ark.
On that day, the flood came.
The flood destroyed everyone.
The days of the Son of Man will be like the days of Noah.
People will live their normal lives.
Then sudden judgment will come.
passages.original: Καὶ καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Νῶε οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἤσθιον ἔπινον ἐγάμουν ἐγαμίζοντο ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας

passages.text: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.
passages.sermon:
In the days of Lot, people lived their normal lives.
They ate food.
They drank.
They bought things.
They sold things.
They planted crops.
They built houses.
Life continued as usual for them.
passages.original: Ὁμοίως καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Λώτ ἤσθιον ἔπινον ἠγόραζον ἐπώλουν ἐφύτευον ᾠκοδόμουν

passages.text: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.
passages.sermon:
Lot was a righteous man.
Lot lived in Sodom.
One day, Lot left Sodom.
On that day, fire fell from heaven.
Sulfur also fell from heaven.
The fire and sulfur came down on Sodom.
The fire and sulfur destroyed everyone in Sodom.
passages.original: ᾗ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ἐξῆλθεν Λὼτ ἀπὸ Σοδόμων ἔβρεξεν πῦρ καὶ θεῖον ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας

passages.text: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God will reveal Jesus on a certain day.
On that day, events will happen just like in the days of Lot.
People will live their normal lives.
Sudden judgment will come.
passages.original: Κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ ἔσται ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκαλύπτεται

passages.text: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.
passages.sermon:
Jesus warned about the day when the Son of Man will be revealed.
On that day, some people will be on the housetop.
Their possessions will be inside the house.
They must not go down to get their possessions.
Some people will be in the field.
They must not turn back for anything they left behind.
passages.original: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὃς ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι αὐτά καὶ ὁ ἐν ἀγρῷ ὁμοίως μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω

passages.text: Remember Lot’s wife!
passages.sermon:
Lot’s wife lived in the time of Sodom and Gomorrah.
God destroyed those cities because of their great sin.
God told Lot and his family to flee and not look back.
Lot’s wife looked back at the city.
God turned her into a pillar of salt.
Remember Lot’s wife.
passages.original: μνημονεύετε τῆς γυναικὸς Λώτ

passages.text: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples about the coming day of judgment.
He warned them about what would happen.
He said, “Whoever tries to save his own life will lose it.”
He also said, “Whoever loses his life will keep it alive.”
passages.original: ὃς ἐὰν ζητήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ περιποιήσασθαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ ζωογονήσει αὐτήν

passages.text: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: One will be taken and the other left.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He warned them about the coming judgment.
He said, “I tell you this.”
On that night, two people will share one bed.
One person will be taken.
The other person will be left.
passages.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἔσονται δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς ὁ εἷς παραλημφθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται

passages.text: Two women will be grinding grain together: One will be taken and the other left.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the coming judgment.
He described a situation with two women.
Both women will be grinding grain together.
One woman will be taken.
The other woman will be left.
passages.original: ἔσονται δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα ἀφεθήσεται

passages.text: “Where, Lord?” they asked. Jesus answered, “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
The disciples asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Where, Lord?”
Jesus answered them.
He said, “Wherever there is a dead body, the vultures will gather.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ποῦ Κύριε Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα ἐκεῖ καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται
